questions.stem: He is ashamed ___ his conduct.
questions.explanation: 'Ashamed of' is the fixed collocation.

questions.stem: He was charged ___ murder.
questions.explanation: 'Charge somebody WITH' a crime; 'accuse somebody OF' it.

questions.stem: He is bent ___ doing mischief.
questions.explanation: 'Bent on' means determined to do something.

questions.stem: This decision is contrary ___ the rule.
questions.explanation: 'Contrary to' is the standard form.

questions.stem: She is anxious ___ her son's health.
questions.explanation: 'Anxious about' means worried about something.

questions.stem: I am indebted ___ you for your help.
questions.explanation: 'Indebted to' a person is the fixed pattern.

questions.stem: He is eligible ___ the post.
questions.explanation: 'Eligible for' a post or benefit.

questions.stem: They are satisfied ___ the result.
questions.explanation: 'Satisfied with' is the standard collocation.

questions.stem: He is popular ___ the students.
questions.explanation: 'Popular with' a group of people.

questions.stem: By next June he ___ here for five years.
questions.explanation: A duration completed by a future point takes the future perfect continuous.

questions.stem: They ___ the matter for an hour now.
questions.explanation: 'For an hour now' with a continuing action takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.stem: The train ___ before we got to the station.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past events takes the past perfect.

questions.stem: If I ___ enough money, I would buy the house.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: 'if + past tense' with 'would + base verb'.

questions.stem: Do not disturb him while he ___ .
questions.explanation: An action in progress right now takes the present continuous.

questions.stem: I ___ here since my childhood.
questions.explanation: 'Since' with a state continuing to the present takes the present perfect.

questions.stem: By the end of this year she ___ ten years of service.
questions.explanation: An action finished before a future point takes the future perfect.

questions.stem: He ___ football every Friday.
questions.explanation: A habitual action takes the simple present with -s for a singular subject.

questions.stem: She said she ___ busy at that moment.
questions.explanation: The present tense back-shifts to the past after a past reporting verb.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'One cannot deny this fact.'
options: This fact has not been denied.
questions.explanation: An indefinite subject is dropped and the modal becomes 'cannot be + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'They elected him president.'
options: He is elected president by them.
questions.explanation: With a factitive object the complement 'president' stays after the passive verb.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'Who broke the window?'
options: By whom the window was broken?
By whom was the window broken?
questions.explanation: In a passive question the auxiliary precedes the subject.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'Help the poor.'
options: Help should be given the poor.
questions.explanation: An imperative becomes 'Let + object + be + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'She teaches us English.'
options: English is taught us by her.
We are taught English by her.
questions.explanation: With two objects the indirect object usually becomes the passive subject.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'They have built a new house.'
options: A new house is built by them.
A new house has been built by them.
A new house was built by them.
A new house had been built by them.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active becomes 'has/have been + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'The boy is reading a book.'
options: A book is read by the boy.
A book is being read by the boy.
A book was being read by the boy.
A book has been read by the boy.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active becomes 'is/are being + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'The storm destroyed the crops.'
options: The crops destroyed by the storm.
The crops were destroyed by the storm.
The crops are destroyed by the storm.
The crops have destroyed by the storm.
questions.explanation: Simple past active becomes 'was/were + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'The gardener waters the plants.'
options: The plants are watered by the gardener.
The plants were watered by the gardener.
The plants water by the gardener.
The plants have watered by the gardener.
questions.explanation: Simple present active becomes 'is/are + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'We saw him in the park.'
options: He saw by us in the park.
He was seen by us in the park.
He is seen by us in the park.
He has seen by us in the park.
questions.explanation: Simple past active becomes 'was/were + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into active: 'The song was sung by her.'
questions.explanation: 'Was + past participle' corresponds to the simple past active.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I have finished my work."
options: He said that he has finished his work.
He said that he had finished his work.
He said that he finished his work.
He said that he was finishing his work.
questions.explanation: The present perfect shifts to the past perfect in reported speech.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: The boy said, "Sir, may I come in?"
options: The boy asked sir if he might come in.
The boy respectfully asked if he might come in.
The boy said sir that he may come in.
The boy told sir to come in.
questions.explanation: 'Sir' becomes an adverb of respect, and 'may' becomes 'might'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "What a fine day it is!"
options: He said that it was a fine day.
He exclaimed that it was a very fine day.
He asked what a fine day it was.
He exclaimed what a fine day it is.
questions.explanation: An exclamatory sentence becomes assertive with 'exclaimed that' and an intensifier.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: She said, "We went there last week."
options: She said that they went there last week.
She said that they had gone there the previous week.
She said that they have gone there last week.
She said that they would go there the previous week.
questions.explanation: Simple past becomes past perfect; 'last week' becomes 'the previous week'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "Are you ill?"
options: She asked him if he was ill.
She asked him if he is ill.
She said him whether he was ill.
She asked him was he ill.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if' and a back-shifted verb.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Do not tell a lie."
options: He advised me not to tell a lie.
He said me not to tell a lie.
He asked me that I do not tell a lie.
He told me do not tell a lie.
questions.explanation: A negative imperative giving counsel becomes 'advised … not to + verb'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Bring me a glass of water."
options: He told me to bring him a glass of water.
He said me to bring him a glass of water.
He asked me bringing him a glass of water.
He told me that bring him a glass of water.
questions.explanation: An imperative becomes 'told + object + to-infinitive', with pronouns adjusted.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I am not well today."
options: She said that she is not well today.
She said that she was not well that day.
She said that she was not well today.
She told that she is not well that day.
questions.explanation: The verb back-shifts and 'today' becomes 'that day'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "You can go now."
options: He said that I can go now.
He said that I could go then.
He told that I can go then.
He asked me to go now.
questions.explanation: 'Can' becomes 'could' and 'now' becomes 'then'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: Father said, "The sun rises in the east."
options: Father said that the sun rose in the east.
Father said that the sun rises in the east.
Father told that the sun rose in the east.
Father said that the sun had risen in the east.
questions.explanation: A universal truth keeps its present tense in reported speech.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I was reading a novel."
options: He said that he was reading a novel.
He said that he had been reading a novel.
He said that he is reading a novel.
He said that he read a novel.
questions.explanation: The past continuous shifts to the past perfect continuous.

questions.stem: ‘সে না এলে আমি যাব না’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: I will not go if he will not come.
I will not go unless he comes.
I will not go unless he does not come.
I do not go unless he come.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' নিজেই নেতিবাচক, তাই এর পরে আবার 'not' বসে না।

questions.stem: ‘সে স্কুলে যাওয়ার আগে খেয়েছিল’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: He ate before he went to school.
He had eaten before he went to school.
He has eaten before he went to school.
He eats before he goes to school.
questions.explanation: দুটি অতীত কাজের মধ্যে আগেরটিতে past perfect বসে।

questions.stem: ‘আমি তোমাকে দেখে খুশি হয়েছি’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: I am glad to see you.
I am glad for see you.
questions.explanation: আবেগসূচক বিশেষণের পরে to-infinitive বসে।

questions.stem: ‘আমি কখনো মিথ্যা বলি না’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: I do never tell a lie.
I am never telling a lie.
questions.explanation: 'Never' নিজেই নেতিবাচক; 'tell a lie' প্রচলিত বাগ্‌ভঙ্গি।

questions.stem: ‘এটা কার বই?’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: মালিকানা জানতে চাইলে 'Whose' ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.stem: ‘সময় নষ্ট করো না’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: নেতিবাচক আদেশে 'Do not + base verb' বসে।

questions.stem: ‘সে কী করছে?’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: প্রশ্নে সহায়ক ক্রিয়া কর্তার আগে বসে।

questions.stem: ‘তার একটি বাড়ি আছে’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: অধিকার বোঝাতে 'has' ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.stem: ‘আজ খুব গরম’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: আবহাওয়া বোঝাতে অস্তিত্ববাচক 'It' কর্তা হিসেবে বসে।

questions.stem: ‘তারা দুই ভাই’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: বহুবচন কর্তার সঙ্গে 'are' এবং বহুবচন বিশেষ্য বসে।

questions.stem: ‘সে আমার চেয়ে ভালো’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: He is more good than me.
questions.explanation: 'Good'-এর তুলনামূলক রূপ 'better', এবং তুলনায় 'than' বসে।

questions.stem: 'To have an axe to grind' means —
questions.explanation: It means to have a private or selfish interest in a matter.

questions.stem: 'A wild goose chase' means —
questions.explanation: It means a hopeless search or pursuit of something unattainable.

questions.stem: 'To keep body and soul together' means —
questions.explanation: It means to earn just enough to stay alive.

questions.stem: 'To burn one's fingers' means —
questions.explanation: It means to get into trouble by interfering in something.

questions.stem: 'To hit the nail on the head' means —
options: To say exactly the right thing
questions.explanation: It means to identify or state something precisely.

questions.stem: 'The lion's share' means —
questions.explanation: It means the biggest or best portion of something.

questions.stem: 'To be in hot water' means —
questions.explanation: It means to be in difficulty or facing trouble.

questions.stem: 'To take after' someone means —
questions.explanation: 'Take after' means to resemble an older relative in looks or character.

questions.stem: 'To call it a day' means —
options: To stop working for the day
questions.explanation: It means to decide to stop working for the time being.

questions.stem: 'The last straw' means —
options: The final small burden that causes collapse
questions.explanation: From 'the last straw that breaks the camel's back' — the final trouble one can bear.

questions.stem: He suggested ___ there together.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund, not a to-infinitive.

questions.stem: He avoided ___ my question.
questions.explanation: 'Avoid' takes a gerund.

questions.stem: He stopped ___ two years ago.
questions.explanation: 'Stop + gerund' means to give up the habit; 'stop to smoke' would mean pausing in order to smoke.

questions.stem: I remember ___ him somewhere before.
questions.explanation: 'Remember + gerund' refers to a past memory; 'remember to' refers to a future duty.

questions.stem: They decided ___ the city.
questions.explanation: 'Decide' is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.stem: He refused ___ the offer.
questions.explanation: 'Refuse' takes a to-infinitive.

questions.stem: She enjoys ___ in her free time.
questions.explanation: 'Enjoy' is always followed by a gerund.

questions.stem: They finished ___ the house last week.
questions.explanation: 'Finish' takes a gerund.

questions.stem: He agreed ___ me with the project.
questions.explanation: 'Agree' is followed by a to-infinitive.

questions.stem: In 'He hurt himself while playing', the word 'himself' is a —
questions.explanation: A pronoun turning the action back on the subject is a reflexive pronoun.

questions.stem: In 'Two boys came late', the word 'two' is a —
questions.explanation: A word stating how many is a numeral adjective.

questions.stem: In 'Poverty is a curse', the word 'poverty' is a —
questions.explanation: A condition that cannot be perceived by the senses is an abstract noun.

questions.stem: In 'He is the best boy in the class', the word 'best' is a —
questions.explanation: It is the superlative degree of 'good' qualifying the noun 'boy'.

questions.stem: In 'Whose book is this?', the word 'whose' is a —
questions.explanation: It asks a question in place of a noun, so it is an interrogative pronoun.

questions.stem: In 'Man is mortal', the word 'man' is a —
questions.explanation: It names a class of beings, so it is a common noun.

questions.stem: In 'She sings well', the word 'well' is a —
questions.explanation: It modifies the verb 'sings', so it is an adverb of manner.

questions.stem: In 'Water is a liquid', the word 'water' is a —
questions.explanation: A noun naming a substance is a material noun.

questions.stem: In 'The committee has met', the word 'committee' is a —
questions.explanation: A word naming a body of people taken as one unit is a collective noun.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: He gave me a piece of advice.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable, so it takes 'a piece of' rather than 'an'.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: He is taller than any boy in the class.
He is taller than any other boy in the class.
He is tallest than any other boy.
He is more tall than any other boy.
questions.explanation: Comparing a member with its own group requires 'any OTHER', or the sentence compares him with himself.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Acquaintance' keeps the 'cqu' of 'acquaint' and ends in -ance.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Rhythm' has an 'h' after both r and t, and no vowel between th and m.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Exaggerate' has a double g.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Colleague' ends in -eague, like 'league'.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Grammar' ends in -ar, not -er.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: He is absent in the class.
He is absent from the class.
He is absent of the class.
He is absent at the class.
questions.explanation: 'Absent from' is the fixed collocation.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'tenacious'.
questions.explanation: 'Tenacious' means holding firmly, persistent.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'audacious'.
questions.explanation: 'Audacious' means showing a willingness to take bold risks.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'generous'.
questions.explanation: 'Generous' means free in giving; 'miserly' means unwilling to give.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'artificial'.
questions.explanation: 'Artificial' means man-made; its opposite is 'natural'.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'reluctant'.
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means hesitant or unwilling.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'commence'.
questions.explanation: 'Commence' means to begin.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'permanent'.
questions.explanation: 'Permanent' means lasting; 'temporary' means for a limited time.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'praise'.
questions.explanation: 'Praise' and 'blame' are direct opposites.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'cruel'.
questions.explanation: 'Cruel' and 'kind' are direct opposites.
